learning: Hypothesis A: narrower track raises turn authority, lifting oval progress above 0.1175 and lowering max_error below 0.06. Hypothesis B: the extra yaw over-responds, raising s-bend and slalom oscillation without a progress gain.
notes: Integration change: none to the controller. Only wheel_track moves from 0.12 to 0.10 m, as the Builder asked. Expect roughly 20% more turn rate per unit of wheel-speed difference, so watch s-bend steering_oscillation against the 0.15 limit.
rationale: Iteration 3 is the best result so far (54.90). Its gain came from the s-bend and slalom, while oval progress stayed flat at 0.1175 with max_error at the 0.06 m off-track floor. The Builder's iteration 4 proposal changes one thing: wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m. Geometry is otherwise unchanged from iteration 3: 16 mm sensors, x = -0.08 to 0.08 at 0.04 m spacing, y = 0.07, wheel radius 0.03, mass 0.8, body 0.16 by 0.14. The controller is also unchanged from iteration 3 (kp 3.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.2, base_speed 2.0, sensor_weights -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, line_loss last_direction), so the race isolates the track change. Turn rate per unit of wheel-speed difference rises by about 0.12/0.10 = 1.2x, so the same kp produces about 20% more yaw. I am not adding a gain change to keep the test clean, and I expect the s-bend oscillation to rise (iteration 3 was 0.144). I am keeping the existing controller because no telemetry from this geometry exists yet. Expected: oval progress above 0.1175 with max_error below 0.06, s-bend and slalom progress at or above iteration 3, and s-bend steering_oscillation below about 0.15.
